criteria.evidence: Config and ticket templates contain blank fields. AC1 tests exercise copying config into new tickets and reviewerSettings override/fallback behaviour.
runCodexReview omits unset arguments. AC2 tests inspect captured arguments and scan code, templates and skills for hard-coded model names.

The Codex test exercises initial and resumed argument construction. The Claude test checks documentation keywords and reviewer-settings output, but does not exercise reviewer creation. The builder's description of available tool parameters establishes plausibility, not a behavioural test.
lintTicket validates ticket and config effort values. AC4 tests cover allowed and invalid efforts and unrestricted model names.

cmdReviewerSettings now persists starting settings and cmdRecord reuses them. The new AC5 regression changes ticket settings between recorded rounds and verifies both retain their original metadata. Existing tests cover default metadata and pack output.

findings.issue: The dispute correctly explains why a Node unit test cannot directly invoke Claude's Agent tool, but the claimed Claude behaviour still has no test exercising it. The existing test's title overstates what its documentation checks establish.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide a reproducible integration or manual smoke test that follows the skill to start a Claude reviewer with supported configured model and effort values, and with both unset. Record the actual invocation and successful result. This need not be a Node unit test or validate arbitrary model names.

findings.issue: Recorded resumed-subagent rounds previously used current ticket settings rather than the reviewer's starting settings. The persisted settings and regression test address this.
findings.suggested_fix: No further change required for the reported scenario.

product_md.note: The saved-settings fix supports the review-history description, and the new alias limitation clarifies the Claude input format. Claude execution remains unverified, consistent with the existing end-to-end testing limitation.

verdict.summary: The review-history bug is fixed and covered by a regression test. Codex settings have useful coverage. One gap remains: demonstrate that the Claude reviewer can actually be started using the skill's configured and default settings. Sandbox startup still prevents independent repository reads or test execution; this assessment uses the supplied diffs and test output.
